status: Software implementation and scoped admission complete. Physical GPU results, real GPU concurrency/coherency/performance and conformance remain deferred in OssiGPU.txt /0.79.36; WSI follows in 0.79.37.

implementation: Independent and linked SPIR-V shader objects execute the original frontend in isolated CPU jobs. Bounded diagnostics are delivered after join. Serialized NIR and embedded sampler CPU arrays remain owned until backend compilation completes; no interned type or Vulkan callback allocation crosses owners.

Original driver backend compiles each stage through its existing private NIR/NAK worker. Shader creation/uploads and original linked rollback remain on the caller. Successful frontend owners are destroyed on every completion branch, including later frontend/backend failures.
EXT_shader_object and shaderObject follow the upstream supported class again. Generated commands and all three pipeline library/binary extensions remain filtered pending their separate integration.
checks: Normal 512-unit native C build, original verified NIL/NAK and generated C/Zig ABI pass; mandatory linked symbols resolve.
Independent public C consumer loads normal R4VK.R4L from the standard image plan. Validated SPIR-V VS/FS stages compile independently and linked in reversed order.

Binary export/import/re-export is byte-identical. Short export preserves the destination and returns INCOMPLETE. Corrupted magic, driver, UUID, version, length and hash or truncated header return INCOMPATIBLE_SHADER_BINARY; retry succeeds.

Four exact callback allocation failures cover each linked shader object/push allocation, including rollback after a previous stage was compiled and uploaded. All callbacks balance after error and successful retry. Independent create batches publish valid/null outputs and continue after a rejected binary.

Public compute shader specialization 7=41, storage-buffer descriptor, transfer-to-compute barrier, bind/dispatch(32,1,1)/unbind and modeled submit/fence/cleanup pass. Before model activation bootfb blit works; broker reset gives DEVICE_LOST and new instance/device succeeds.
limitations: No GPU instructions execute in the modeled backend. Real CPU compilation, allocation, upload and native broker ownership are exercised; GPU raster/compute values and physical cache visibility remain OssiGPU.txt follow-ups.
This scoped checkpoint covers VS/FS creation and compute dispatch, not full graphics rendering, geometry/tessellation/mesh runtime, all shader-object dynamic state or full 0.79.36 admission.

OOM counts prove callback-object rollback. Existing unchanged compiler-job/heap isolation and abort tests are reused from 0.79.35; no claim of a fresh total internal budget/concurrency proof. No new permanent test group.

implementation: Original DGC init/process NIR builders and indirect-copy helper use nvk_compile_meta_shader_native. Only CPU scalars/serialized NIR cross worker boundaries; Vulkan callbacks, GPU upload, cache publication and rollback stay on the caller.

Process stride/QMD size is published into the layout after successful compilation. EXT_device_generated_commands and dynamicGeneratedPipelineLayout use original supported class flags. KHR indirectMemoryCopy is usable; indirectMemoryToImageCopy stays false.
checks: Canonical 512-unit native build plus original NIL/NAK and generated C/Zig ABI; linked mandatory symbols resolve. Standard image plan installs R4VK 0.1.5 exactly once.
Independent C consumer verifies DGC/copy/BDA/maintenance5 features and extension admission. Compute shader object is indirect-bindable; shader execution set creates two slots and updates index 1.

Three callback OOMs at layout/process/init shader allocations return OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY and balance all callback objects, including previously uploaded process shader. Successful retry allocates/frees three objects.

Actual generated-command memory requirements and aligned native BDA buffers; explicit preprocess, preprocess-write/indirect-read barrier, then execute. Count=1 with maxSequenceCount=2 uses one active and one inactive sequence. Separate implicit preprocess layout/buffer range uses maxSequenceCount=1 and no count address; shader rebinding and compute barrier avoid cross-dispatch write hazards.

Original graphics token builder compiles pushconstant, sequence-index, vertex-buffer, index-buffer and indexed-draw tokens with dynamic pipeline-layout info. Layout creation/destruction only; no graphics draw is submitted by this case.

Two disjoint indirect memory copies run fresh and cached helper paths; zero copy count is accepted. Native modeled submit/fence completes, resources are destroyed, broker reset returns DEVICE_LOST, replacement device and bootfb fallback pass.
limitations: GPU-generated command data and GPU copy/compute output are not executed or compared in the model. Native CPU compilation, RAM/upload, metadata and broker lifetimes are exercised. Physical correctness/coherency remains in OssiGPU.txt.

Initial exploratory guest passed but is not accepted: two active compute sequences wrote the same storage buffer without an inner dependency. Final fixture uses one active sequence, adds implicit preprocessing and uses separate preprocess ranges with required barriers. Both logs and artifacts are retained. Patch-context normalization changes build identity but leaves prepared C byte-identical.

Callback OOM accounting is scoped; this is not a full internal budget/concurrency/graphics admission. Pipeline libraries/binaries, remaining graphics/compute feature integration and whole-scope error/budget qualification remain open. No new permanent gate.

implementation: Native pipeline binary loading preserves deserializer/upload result codes through the existing cache owner. Optional cache insertion can still return a usable uncached object; no duplicate ownership model.

Compute binary import initializes cache_hit=false. Too-short graphics binary lists leave through stage cleanup instead of continuing pipeline construction (defensive invalid-input handling, not a valid-usage conformance claim).

Shared native shader upload checks vk_device_check_status before using a retained heap mapping. A cached block must not bypass broker-generation/device-loss detection; upload errors propagate through shader deserialization and binary pipeline creation.

KHR_pipeline_library, EXT_graphics_pipeline_library and KHR_pipeline_binary expose original class support. Retained precompiled NIR uses the existing isolated frontend/backend. pipelineBinaryInternalCache and its control properties remain false; no missing disk cache is advertised.
checks: Canonical 512-unit native build, original NIL/NAK, generated C/Zig ABI and ELF/R4M relocation checks; ordinary image plan contains R4VK 0.1.6 once.

Independent public C consumer: four graphics library subsets; VS and FS retained-NIR plus compiled-shader binary capture/import with modules absent. Fast and optimized LTO links then destroy libraries before recording actual triangle draws.

Standalone VS/FS pipeline capture/export/import and draw; stable global and graphics pipeline keys. Binary count query and short handle array return INCOMPLETE without touching the sentinel. Short byte export returns NOT_ENOUGH_SPACE and required length without writing; imported keys/bytes re-export identically.

Callback OOM at both entries of a two-binary import and at the compute binary import returns per-entry nulls, completes other outputs, balances callback ownership and retries. Graphics link allocation failure returns null; successful links follow.
Compute pipeline binary import records storage-buffer specialization 7=41, dispatch(32,1,1), required barrier and valid non-cache-hit creation feedback. Modeled submission/fence and cleanup complete.
Kernel broker reset leaves the old device lost; compute binary reimport propagates DEVICE_LOST with null output. Binary/layout cleanup, replacement device and actual CPU bootfb fallback succeed.
limitations: The broker does not execute GPU instructions. Draw pixels, compute results, physical memory coherency and Vulkan conformance are not proven. Exact real-GPU resumption steps are in OssiGPU.txt.

The first guest passed library, binary and command checks but failed DEVICE_LOST on reimport. A retained shader heap bypassed native allocation/status checks. First logs/artifacts/source patch are retained; final run adds the shared upload status check.

Callback accounting is bounded and is not full internal pressure/concurrency qualification. Vertex/index inputs, textures, further graphics stages, depth/stencil/blending, storage images and whole-scope budget/failure admission remain open. No permanent gate added.

version: ESSL Version: OpenGL ES GLSL 3.20 glslang Khronos. 15.2.0

implementation: Native image requirements reserve whole plane binding pages and include that padding before later planes and zcull. Stencil-copy temporary planes use the native binding alignment when they have a PTE kind. Non-native Mesa behavior remains unchanged.

Precompiled shader payload validation includes task and mesh stages; the legacy MESA_SHADER_STAGES limit ended at compute. Native frontend transfer preserves the deserializer result instead of reporting every failure as host OOM.

Original NVK vertex/index, descriptor, sampler, renderpass/dynamic-rendering, depth/stencil/blend, geometry/tessellation/mesh/task and storage-image paths use the existing isolated NIL/NIR/NAK integration and native resource owners.
checks: Canonical native build, original NIL/NAK, generated C/Zig ABI and ELF/R4M relocation checks. All nine GLSL-derived SPIR-V modules pass spirv-val for Vulkan 1.3.

Independent public consumer: sampled RGBA8 texture, UBO, push constants, vertex/index buffer, RGBA8 target and D32S8 attachment. Six compiled graphics pipelines cover legacy and dynamic rendering plus geometry, tessellation, mesh and task/mesh stages.

Seven independently cleared render passes include a generated indexed draw with vertex/index/pushconstant tokens and original GPU preprocessing. Each target is copied to a separate host buffer interval.

Final render target feeds a storage-image compute shader through the graphics/compute barrier. Dispatch writes a channel-permuted output image and packed source colors to a storage buffer; output-image copy and GPU/host barrier are recorded.

Model checks real CPU-recorded NVIDIA packet encoding: indexed/mesh draw arguments and enabled depth/stencil/blending. Native resource coverage, submit/fence, destruction, broker reset, DEVICE_LOST, replacement device and actual CPU bootfb fallback complete.
limitations: The first guest hit a real nvkmd binding bounds assertion. An instrumented rerun localized it to D32S8 binding; both failed logs/artifacts are retained.

The image-fixed guest reached geometry and tessellation but rejected mesh precompiled data at the legacy stage bound. The corrected module with the identical consumer records every scene stage. Intermediate patches/modules/logs are retained.

The CPU decoder initially requested an ordinary CPU map during active native GPU ownership and prevented completion. The fixture now obtains the RAM address at binding creation, retained by the live canonical binding reference, and inspects CPU-recorded bytes as a modeled GPU reader while the native job is active. No production CPU/BO hazard rules change. The final consumer adds only a completion marker after the model validates its counters.

The model executes no GPU instruction, including generated commands. Raster pixels, depth/stencil values, storage-image/buffer contents and physical cache coherency remain unverified. Exact readback procedure is in OssiGPU.txt.

The scoped command decoder checks selected CPU-recorded methods, not the complete command ISA or Vulkan conformance. Full budget/concurrency and feature/failure admission remain open. No permanent test group added.

implementation: Descriptor-pool products are widened before multiplication; checked uint64 additions reject overflow. An empty heap is initialized before backing allocation so its destructor is valid on OOM. Ordinary pool sizes and original allocation/rollback behavior are retained.

Original meta color/depth/stencil resolve uses isolated frontend/backend compilation, native image planes and resource/queue owners. Native resource budgets and generation-bound device-lost remain shared by every path.
checks: Canonical native build, generated C/Zig ABI, ELF and R4M relocation checks; independent public C consumer in SMP4.

Two valid oversized descriptor-pool requests reject with DEVICE_OOM instead of wrapping uint32 products. Partial set allocation nulls every output and rolls back; free, reset and pool destruction permit reuse. Callback pool/sampler OOM and four sampler cycles balance callback allocations.

Two application threads overlap compute-pipeline creation using one internally synchronized explicit cache, distinct specializations and subsequent cache hits. Pipelines remain usable after cache/module destruction; both dispatches are recorded.

MSAA4 RGBA8 average and D32S8 sample-zero dynamic rendering resolve, explicit CmdResolveImage2, separate color/depth/stencil readback ranges and GPU/host barriers. The model decodes real six-vertex meta-draw arguments (at least three) and validates native resource coverage.

Submit/fence, complete resource destruction, broker reset, public DEVICE_LOST, replacement device, and exact BO/reference/lease/backing/pinning/mapping/budget return to the pre-device baseline; actual CPU bootfb fallback.
limitations: The first pressure probe faulted in util_vma_heap_finish because backing allocation failure destroyed an uninitialized pool heap. Fault offset, module, source and logs are archived; the consumer and model driver remain byte-identical for the corrected rerun.
Model GPU completion does not execute commands or validate pixels, compute values, multisample arithmetic or real cache coherency. Hardware recipe is OssiGPU /0.79.36.
Cache API calls overlap on real SMP threads; the probe does not require simultaneous NAK instructions or measure physical GPU concurrency. No conformance or performance claim.

The selected descriptor/sampler and pipeline cases are bounded, not exhaustive. Earlier compiler/cache/queue fault and pressure evidence is reused with explicit source comparisons. Historical changed files in older checkpoints are superseded by the later 0.79.35 resource/command proofs and current 0.79.36 paths.
Guest image carries release 0.79.35; only the distribution release stamp advances after admission. No new permanent test group.

tasks.scope: Isolated SPIR-V/NIR/NAK, all graphics/compute stages and generation-checked upload.
Original vertex/index/texture, renderpass/dynamic, depth/stencil/blend, copy and resolve command integration.
Storage images/buffers, dispatch, barriers and queue dependencies; GPU values deferred.

Explicit pipeline/cache creation and pooled descriptors; lazy meta creation belongs to preparation/first command recording, never a present-time compiler. WSI integration must warm required paths before steady presentation.

Exact admitted GA/AD identities feed original NVK/NIL/NAK class/format tables. Native filter removes unavailable host features; newly exposed optional paths are implemented and exercised. Device API1.3, instance1.4, no inherited CTS qualification.

Isolated compiler OOM/abort returns truthful errors before submit; recoverable OOM permits retry. Native execution failure/reset propagates shared device-lost and retains resources until confirmed retirement.

budget_review: Sampler table: 4096 slots, advertised max4000; image descriptors: initial1024, maximum1048576; descriptor pools are explicit bounded allocations.

Shader heap/VA/BO allocations are admitted by native owners. Implicit device pipeline cache holds weak references; explicit application caches retain data until their owner destroys them and remain under host allocation budgets.

Per-job compiler arenas reclaim CPU state only after exact join. Queue push/dependency limits, pressure rollback and late resource retirement use the unchanged common owners; no detached per-frame compiler owner is added.
feature_review: Sparse/replay, external FD/dmabuf/DRM, placed maps, calibrated GPU timestamps, memory-budget telemetry and HDR metadata are not advertised. WSI/swapchain remains unbuilt until0.79.37.

NIL format predicates gate sampling/filtering, color/blend, depth/stencil and storage; atomics match actual enabled shader capabilities. Linear depth/stencil and unsupported blocks are rejected. Class/SM facts are validated against R4NV, not inferred from PCI vendor alone.

Shader objects, generated commands, pipeline libraries/binaries and all graphics stages now use the real native compile/upload path. Memory-to-image indirect copy remains false. No extension is enabled solely because its upstream Linux implementation exists.
software_admission.acceptance: A1: scoped compiler/data/reference and command/synchronization integration; A2: real SMP pipeline/cache concurrency plus native owner fault/pressure/retirement and exact BO budget return. Physical parts remain OssiGPU /0.79.36 A1/A2.
